Slomniki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Słomniki, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first recorded in Słomniki in the 16th century, though significant settlement developed only after 1863; by 1921, 1,460 (30.4%) were mostly murdered at Bełżec in 1942. This cemetery, established in 1898, held an unknown number of Jews murdered during the town's deportation between August 28-September 2, 1942, and was devastated around the same time; Poland formally closed it on November 4, 1964. A 1960s monument marked the mass grave; 1998-1999 restoration by the Nissenbaum Family Foundation, the Association of Jews from Słomniczów in Israel, and the town hall added fencing and Holocaust memorials, followed by a 2020 volunteer cleanup led by Maria Górowska. No pre-war tombstones survive, though four black granite stelae bearing Słomniki Jews' names were placed at the entrance in 1998; destroyed matzevot excavated from the town market in 2014 are preserved at the local Land Museum.
